## 1. The manifest (manifest.toml)

Its JSON Schema is [manifest.schema.json](manifest.schema.json), generated with this file. The host ignores a key it does not know (`npm run plugin:check` warns about one), and from 1.4 leaves out a list value it does not know, with a warning on the plugin's Settings row. "Since" is the host API version that added a key; declare at least that `api_version` to use it.

```toml test
key = "hello-workspace"
name = "Hello workspace"
version = "0.1.0"
api_version = "1.4"
license = "GPL-3.0-or-later"
description = "One study kind with its own page"
authors = ["Your Name"]

[[workspaces]]
key = "hello"
title = "Hello"
entry = "workspace/index.html"

[[study_kinds]]
key = "hello"
title = "Hello"
workspace = "hello"
schema_version = 1
```

### Top-level keys

| Key | Type | Default | Since | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | string |  |  | The plugin's id, the same as its folder name. Letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-'. (matches `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,120}$`; required) |
| `name` | string |  |  | The name Settings → Plugins shows. (required) |
| `version` | string | `"0.0.0"` |  | The plugin's own version; another plugin's requires_plugins compares it. (matches `^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*([-+][0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$`; required) |
| `api_version` | string | `"1.0"` |  | The host API the plugin is written for, major.minor. A host loads it only when the major version matches its own; a later minor version only adds things. (matches `^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$`; required) |
| `license` | string |  |  | SPDX licence expression: GPL-3.0-or-later, or a licence compatible with it. (required) |
| `description` | string | `""` |  | One sentence for the plugin's Settings row. |
| `authors` | string or array of string |  |  | A list of names, or one string of names separated by commas. |
| `ui` | string or false or table |  |  | The folder of the plugin's in-page panels (usually "ui"), or a table {dir, entry}. Leave it out when the plugin has none. |
| `ui_entry` | string | `"index.js"` |  | The entry file in the ui folder. A .tsx, .ts or .jsx entry is bundled by the host when served. |
| `overrides` | string or array of string |  |  | kind:key specs this plugin replaces (a list, or one string separated by commas). |
| `requires` | array of tables |  |  | What the plugin needs on this PC (a WSL program, a Python package, a GPU); Settings shows what is missing. |
| `tier` | string |  | 1.1 | Informational: the folder decides the tier (bundled-plugins/ is bundled, plugins/ is user). (one of `"bundled"`, `"user"`) |
| `required` | boolean | `false` | 1.1 | Bundled tier only: the app cannot create or run simulations without it, and it cannot be turned off. |
| `default_enabled` | boolean | `true` | 1.2 | Bundled tier only: false ships the plugin off until someone turns it on in Settings → Plugins. |
| `requires_plugins` | string or array of string |  | 1.1 | Plugins loaded before this one: "key" or "key>=1.0". |
| `protected` | string or array of string |  | 1.1 | Bundled tier only: kind:key specs of this plugin that other plugins may not drop. |
| `default_analysis` | table |  | 1.2 | A required bundled plugin only: the analysis a study gets when none is named (steady, its transient sibling, and the names older studies stored for it), and the name a study gets when none is stored. |
| `study_kinds` | array of tables |  | 1.1 | Project-level studies the plugin owns. |
| `workspaces` | array of tables |  | 1.1 | Full pages the plugin draws in a sandboxed frame. |
| `start_actions` | array of tables |  | 1.4 | Buttons that create a study of a kind and open it in its workspace. |
| `files` | table |  | 1.2 | Size limits for the plugin's own files in a project. |
| `python` | table |  | 1.1 | The plugin's own Python environment, built from its lock file, and its service. |

| `workspace` | string | `""` |  | The key of the [[workspaces]] page that opens a study of this kind. |

| `links_geometry` | boolean | `false` | 1.4 | A study of this kind may link one project geometry (needs a workspace; the call comes with 1.5). |

| Key | Type | Default | Since | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | string |  |  | lower_snake_case, unique in the plugin. (matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,40}$`; required) |
| `title` | string |  |  | The host's header shows it above the page. (at most 80 characters; required) |
| `icon` | string | `""` |  | One SVG path (its d attribute) drawn in a 24×24 box. (matches `^[MmLlHhVvCcSsQqTtAaZz0-9 ,.\-eE]{0,4000}$`) |
| `entry` | string | `"workspace/index.html"` |  | An .html file in the plugin's workspace/ folder, which is all the host serves. (matches `^workspace/.+\.[Hh][Tt][Mm][Ll]$`) |

| Key | Type | Default | Since | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `study_kind` | string |  |  | A [[study_kinds]] key with a workspace; one action per kind. (matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,40}$`; required) |
| `label` | string |  |  | The button's text, one line. (at most 40 characters; required) |
| `hint` | string | `""` |  | A line under or beside the button. (at most 120 characters) |

| `places` | array of string | `["empty_project","header","new_project","home"]` |  | Where the host draws it (default: all). A place this host does not know is left out with a warning. (each one of `"empty_project"`, `"header"`, `"new_project"`, `"home"`) |
| `home_label` | string | `""` |  | Home's text for the button (default: label). (at most 40 characters) |

## 2. The workspace bridge (@magnusim/workspace)

A workspace page runs in a sandboxed frame. The host injects this import map into every workspace page; build your page with these names external (`npm run plugin:new` writes a Vite config that does):

| Import | Served at |
| --- | --- |
| `react` | `/plugin-sdk/react.js` |
| `react-dom/client` | `/plugin-sdk/react-dom-client.js` |
| `react/jsx-runtime` | `/plugin-sdk/jsx-runtime.js` |
| `react/jsx-dev-runtime` | `/plugin-sdk/jsx-dev-runtime.js` |
| `@magnusim/workspace` | `/plugin-sdk/workspace.js` |
| `@magnusim/plugin-ui` | `/plugin-sdk/plugin-ui.js` |

Types: [workspace-sdk.d.ts](workspace-sdk.d.ts) (copy it into your plugin). Example:

```ts test
import { connect } from '@magnusim/workspace';
import { Button } from '@magnusim/plugin-ui';

const ws = await connect();
const study = await ws.study.get();
// Save a field; a stale rev is refused, so pass the one you read.
const saved = await ws.study.update({ width: 2 }, study.rev);
const { id } = await ws.jobs.start('hello_count', { steps: 5 });
const stop = ws.jobs.events(id, (ev) => {
  if (ev.event === 'end') stop();
});
ws.ui.toast(`Saved ${saved.title}`, { kind: 'success' });
export const kitButton = Button;
```

#### connect

```ts
connect(opts?: { timeoutMs?: number; } | undefined): Promise<Workspace>
```

Say hello to the host and get the workspace's context and bridge. Rejects when the page is not a Magnusim workspace or the host does not answer.

#### SDK_VERSION

```ts
const SDK_VERSION: "1.1.0"
```

The bridge's version; a host accepts a workspace built for the same major version.

#### ComputeJob

```ts
interface ComputeJob
```

A plugin case as the page sees it: no paths.

- `id: string`
- `caseRel: string`
- `app: string`
- `nProcs: number`
- `status: ComputeStatus`
- `stage: string | null`: Where a running case is (pre_copy_in, solve, copy, stopping, …); null before it starts.
- `stopping: boolean`: A stop was asked for and the case has not ended yet.
- `ahead: number | null`: How many jobs run or wait before it, or null when it is not queued.
- `createdAt: string | null`
- `startedAt: string | null`
- `finishedAt: string | null`
- `error: string | null`
- `code: string | null`: Why it was refused or did not finish ("has_results", "launch", "lost", …).
- `result: { savedTimes: number[]; lastSaved: number | null; phases: Record<string, number>; writeFormat: string | null; } | null`: Once it has ended: the saved frames' times, the last one, seconds per phase, and how the solver wrote its fields.
- `seq: number`: The last event's number.

#### ConfirmOptions

```ts
interface ConfirmOptions
```

- `title: string`
- `message?: string | undefined`
- `confirmLabel?: string | undefined`: The confirming button's label ("Delete", "Replace", ...).

#### FileInfo

```ts
interface FileInfo
```

A file in this plugin's folder of the project.

- `rel: string`: Its path from the plugin's folder ("meshes/wing.stl"), spelled as on disk.
- `size: number`
- `mtime: string`: When it last changed (ISO-8601, UTC).
- `etag: string`: Changes whenever the file does; pass it as `ifMatch` to act only on the version you read.

#### FileReadOptions

```ts
interface FileReadOptions
```

- `offset?: number | undefined`: The first byte to read (default 0).
- `length?: number | undefined`: How many bytes to read (default: to the end).
- `ifMatch?: string | undefined`: Read only while the file has this etag (else rejects with code "changed").

#### FileWriteOptions

```ts
interface FileWriteOptions
```

- `ifMatch?: string | null | undefined`: A string: replace only the version with this etag. null: only create a file that is not there yet.
- `sha256?: string | undefined`: The data's SHA-256 (hex): the host checks it before the file is replaced.
- `onProgress?: ((done: number, total: number) => void) | undefined`: Called after each chunk has arrived, with the bytes sent so far and the total.
- `signal?: AbortSignal | undefined`: Aborting it stops the write; the file is left as it was.

#### FileWriteResult

```ts
interface FileWriteResult
```

- `sha256: string`: The SHA-256 of what was written (hex).
- `rel: string`: Its path from the plugin's folder ("meshes/wing.stl"), spelled as on disk.
- `size: number`
- `mtime: string`: When it last changed (ISO-8601, UTC).
- `etag: string`: Changes whenever the file does; pass it as `ifMatch` to act only on the version you read.

#### JobEvent

```ts
interface JobEvent
```

- `event: string`

#### PreStep

```ts
interface PreStep
```

One WSL step. `parallel: true` runs it with `mpirun -np N … -parallel`, only between a decomposePar step and the reconstructParMesh step after it, and only for the tools that can run in parallel.

- `tool: PreTool`
- `args?: string[] | undefined`
- `parallel?: boolean | undefined`

#### PromptOptions

```ts
interface PromptOptions
```

- `title: string`
- `label?: string | undefined`
- `value?: string | undefined`
- `confirmLabel?: string | undefined`

#### StudyRecord

```ts
interface StudyRecord
```

A project-level study record (plugins/<key>/studies/<sid>/study.json) plus the plugin's own fields.

- `id: string`
- `kind: string`
- `title: string`
- `schema_version: number`
- `rev: number`
- `plugin: string`
- `plugin_name: string`
- `plugin_version: string`
- `created_at: string`
- `updated_at: string`

#### SubmitOpenFOAM

```ts
interface SubmitOpenFOAM
```

A case the page wrote in its study's folder, to run with OpenFOAM in WSL (host 1.3).

- `caseRel: string`: The case folder inside this study's folder ("cases/c1"). It must not have run before.
- `app: string`: The solver application, as system/controlDict names it; a registered solver.
- `nProcs?: number | undefined`: Ranks for a parallel solve and parallel steps (1 to 64; the host clamps it to the PC).
- `pre?: PreStep[] | undefined`
- `results: { … }`
- `results.kinematicFields: string[]`: Fields the solver writes divided by density; shown multiplied by rho.
- `results.rho?: number | undefined`
- `results.frameFields?: string[] | undefined`: Fields copied back for each saved frame (default U and p).

#### ThemeInfo

```ts
interface ThemeInfo
```

- `name: "light"`
- `stylesheet: string`: The stylesheet with the design tokens and base styles the host serves.

#### Workspace

```ts
interface Workspace
```

- `context: WorkspaceContext`
- `call<T>(method: string, params?: Record<string, unknown> | undefined, transfer?: Transferable[] | undefined): Promise<T>`: Any bridge call by name; the typed helpers below use it. Rejects with the host's message. `transfer` hands buffers over instead of copying them.
- `service<T>(method: string, params?: Record<string, unknown> | undefined): Promise<T>`: Call a method of this plugin's backend (its service, or its in-process methods).
- `study: { … }`
- `study.get(): Promise<StudyRecord>`
- `study.update(patch: Record<string, unknown>, rev: number): Promise<StudyRecord>`: Save fields of this study; `rev` is the one you read (a stale one is refused).
- `data: { … }`
- `data.read<T>(rel: string): Promise<T | null>`: A JSON file from this plugin's folder in the project (null when there is none).
- `data.write(rel: string, doc: unknown): Promise<void>`
- `files: { … }`: Files of any kind in the same folder (`data` is its JSON view). Paths are relative to it; a study's study.json is read-only here, and files go inside a study's folder (studies/<id>/...), never directly in studies/. Rejections carry `.code`: "changed", "too_large", "quota", "study_record", "study_not_found", "invalid_path", "not_found", "plugin_off", ...
- `files.read(rel: string, opts?: FileReadOptions | undefined): Promise<ArrayBuffer | null>`: The file's bytes, or a range of them (null when there is no such file).
- `files.readBlob(rel: string, opts?: FileReadOptions | undefined): Promise<Blob | null>`: As read, as a Blob.
- `files.stat(rel: string): Promise<FileInfo | null>`
- `files.write(rel: string, data: string | ArrayBuffer | Blob | ArrayBufferView<ArrayBufferLike>, opts?: FileWriteOptions | undefined): Promise<FileWriteResult>`: Write a whole file: sent in chunks, and it replaces the old one only once every byte has arrived. A string is written as UTF-8. While the write is on its way, leaving the workspace asks the user first.
- `files.list(prefix?: string | undefined): Promise<FileInfo[]>`: Every file under a folder ("": the plugin's folder), at any depth, sorted by rel.
- `files.delete(rel: string, opts?: { recursive?: boolean; } | undefined): Promise<{ deleted: number; }>`: Delete a file, or a folder with `recursive`; says how many files went.
- `jobs: { … }`
- `jobs.start(kind: string, params?: Record<string, unknown> | undefined): Promise<{ id: string; }>`: Start one of this plugin's job kinds; returns its id.
- `jobs.events(jobId: string, onEvent: (ev: JobEvent) => void): () => void`: Follow a job this workspace started; returns a function that stops listening.
- `jobs.stop(jobId: string): Promise<void>`
- `project: { … }`
- `project.info(): Promise<{ id: string; title: string; units: UnitSystem; }>`
- `ui: { … }`
- `ui.toast(message: string, opts?: { kind?: "info" | "success" | "error"; } | undefined): Promise<void>`
- `ui.confirm(opts: ConfirmOptions): Promise<boolean>`: The app's own question dialog. The app shows one dialog at a time, so this one may wait its turn. Resolves false without showing it when the user has chosen to leave the workspace by then.
- `ui.prompt(opts: PromptOptions): Promise<string | null>`: The app's own name prompt, in turn as confirm: null when cancelled or not shown.
- `nav: { … }`
- `nav.back(): Promise<boolean>`: Close the workspace and go back to the project. While the page is dirty the app asks the user first, and this resolves false if they choose to stay. When the workspace does close, this page unloads, so the promise may never settle.
- `nav.setDirty(dirty: boolean, message?: string | undefined): Promise<void>`: Mark or clear unsaved work (host 1.2). While dirty, every way out of the workspace asks the user first; closing or reloading the browser tab shows the browser's own prompt. `message` is plain text, at most 200 characters after cleaning, shown in the app's dialog after the plugin's name (never in the browser's prompt). The flag belongs to this page load: a reload of the frame, a closed channel or an approved leave clears it, so do not reload your own page while dirty. Clear it after saving, and before nav.back() to leave without a question.
- `compute: { … }`: OpenFOAM cases this study's page writes and runs (host 1.3: check `context.hostVersion`; an older host refuses with code "not_allowed"). A case runs once, from its `0/` folder, on the app's one compute slot, so it may wait in the queue. Refusals carry `.code` ("app_not_allowed", "has_results", "invalid_path", "busy", …).
- `compute.submitOpenFOAM(opts: SubmitOpenFOAM): Promise<{ id: string; ahead: number; existing: boolean; }>`: Queue a case; `existing` when that folder is already queued or running (its id comes back).
- `compute.events(jobId: string, onEvent: (ev: JobEvent) => void): () => void`: Follow a case of this study: first where it is now (queued, start, or end), then each event (stage, pre, ranks, phase, progress, time_saved, warning, end). Returns a function that stops listening.
- `compute.stop(jobId: string, opts?: { force?: boolean; } | undefined): Promise<{ status: string; stopping: boolean; }>`: Stop a case: a queued one leaves the queue; a running one saves its latest frame and ends. Again to stop harder; `force` at once.
- `compute.status(jobId: string): Promise<ComputeJob>`
- `compute.list(): Promise<ComputeJob[]>`: This study's cases, newest first (a reopened page finds its running case here).
- `results: { … }`
- `results.openIn3D(caseRel: string): Promise<{ opened: boolean; }>`: Show a finished case's saved frames in the project's 3D view. The app asks first when other results are on screen, and when the page has unsaved work. Resolves { opened: false } when the user cancels or stays; when it opens, the workspace closes, so the promise may never settle.
- `on(event: "units", fn: (units: UnitSystem) => void): () => void; on(event: "theme", fn: (theme: ThemeInfo) => void): () => void; on(event: "study", fn: (study: StudyRecord) => void): () => void`: Live changes the host pushes. Returns a function that stops listening. `study`: the study changed (renamed in the header, or saved): save next with its `rev`.
- `spawnWorker(url: string | URL): Worker`: Start an ES-module worker. A sandboxed frame cannot start a worker from a URL or a module worker from a blob; this starts a classic blob worker that imports your module. Messages posted before your module has loaded are held and handed to it, in order, once it has.

#### WorkspaceContext

```ts
interface WorkspaceContext
```

- `plugin: string`
- `workspace: string`
- `project: { … }`
- `project.id: string`
- `project.title: string`
- `study: StudyRecord`
- `units: UnitSystem`
- `theme: ThemeInfo`
- `hostVersion: string`: The host's bridge API version ("1.3"). To use a call a later host added, compare it as numbers, major then minor (ws.nav.setDirty needs 1.2, ws.compute and ws.results need 1.3), or catch the refusal: an older host rejects a call it does not know with code "not_allowed".

#### ComputeStatus

```ts
type ComputeStatus = 'queued' | 'running' | 'done' | 'failed' | 'stopped' | 'lost'
```

#### PreTool

```ts
type PreTool = 'blockMesh' | 'gmshToFoam' | 'surfaceFeatureExtract' | 'snappyHexMesh' | 'extrudeMesh' | 'changeDictionary' | 'createPatch' | 'checkMesh' | 'renumberMesh' | 'decomposePar' | 'reconstructParMesh'
```

A WSL step a plugin case may run before its solver (host 1.3; compatibility.md lists their arguments).

#### UnitSystem

```ts
type UnitSystem = 'metric' | 'imperial'
```

## 3. The plugin UI kit (@magnusim/plugin-ui)

Components and helpers that look like the app's own panels, on the design tokens. Types: [plugin-ui.d.ts](plugin-ui.d.ts).

#### Button

```ts
Button(props: ButtonProps): React.JSX.Element
```

The core's panel buttons: primary (Start, Generate), secondary, neutral (Done), link, fix, danger.

#### ColorLegend

```ts
ColorLegend(props: ColorLegendProps): React.JSX.Element
```

A colour scale: the same table the render uses (colormapGradient), with its range under it.

#### colormapGradient

```ts
colormapGradient(name: ColormapName, stops?: number | undefined): string
```

A CSS linear-gradient (left to right) through `stops` evenly spaced entries of the map.

#### colormapRgb

```ts
colormapRgb(name: ColormapName): Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>
```

The map's 256 RGB entries (768 bytes), a new copy on each call.

#### convertQuantity

```ts
convertQuantity(quantity: Quantity, value: number, fromUnit: string, toUnit: string): number
```

#### DisabledReason

```ts
DisabledReason(props: DisabledReasonProps): React.JSX.Element
```

Why something cannot run, with an optional fix (the Run panel's reason).

#### Elapsed

```ts
Elapsed(props: ElapsedProps): React.JSX.Element
```

useElapsed as text.

#### EmptyState

```ts
EmptyState(props: EmptyStateProps): React.JSX.Element
```

What an empty list or chart shows (.hub-empty, .mon-empty).

#### Field

```ts
Field(props: FieldProps): React.JSX.Element | null
```

A settings row: label (and help) on the left, the control on the right, as schema forms draw it.

#### fieldQuantity

```ts
fieldQuantity(schema: unknown): Quantity | null
```

A schema field's quantity (its x-cfddesk.quantity), or null.

#### fieldUnit

```ts
fieldUnit(q: Quantity, units: UnitSystem): string
```

The unit a schema form shows a number field in: length in mm or in, every other quantity in its first (SI) unit, in either system.

#### formatElapsed

```ts
formatElapsed(ms: unknown): string
```

Milliseconds → m:ss, or h:mm:ss from one hour. Not a number: 0:00.

#### formatEta

```ts
formatEta(ms: unknown): string | null
```

Milliseconds left → "< 10s left" or "~m:ss left"; null when unknown.

#### formatSci

```ts
formatSci(value: number | null | undefined): string
```

Tiny and huge magnitudes read as zero in a plain input, so show them as 1.5290e-5.

#### formatSimTime

```ts
formatSimTime(v: unknown, opts?: { noUnit?: boolean; } | undefined): string
```

## 4. magnusim_sdk

The helpers a plugin may import, in the app and in its own environment (standard library only). A plugin's Python code imports only `magnusim_sdk`, `cfddesk.registry` and the standard library. Example (a service method and one request through the service protocol):

```python test
from magnusim_sdk.service import handle, method

@method("area")
def area(params, scope):
    return {"area": params["width"] * params["height"]}

reply = handle('{"id": 1, "method": "area", "params": {"params": {"width": 2, "height": 3}}}')
assert reply["result"] == {"area": 6}, reply
```

### magnusim_sdk

magnusim_sdk: the helpers a Magnusim plugin may use, with no dependencies.

Constants:

- `SDK_VERSION = "1.2.0"`

### magnusim_sdk.data

A plugin's own data in a project: ``projects/<pid>/plugins/<key>/`` (API 1.2).

#### class PluginDataError(ValueError)

A request outside what the plugin's data scope allows.

#### class StaleRevisionError(PluginDataError)

The study changed since the caller read it (its rev is newer).

#### class StudyNotFoundError(PluginDataError)

No such study in this plugin's folder (deleted, or never made).

#### class FileInfo(TypedDict)

One file in a plugin's folder, as the host's file routes return it.

#### version_tuple

```python
version_tuple(version: str) -> tuple[int, ...]
```

#### is_study_record

```python
is_study_record(parts: Sequence[str]) -> bool
```

studies/<sid>/study.json in any spelling Windows opens as that file.

#### is_study_container

```python
is_study_container(parts: Sequence[str]) -> bool
```

``studies`` or ``studies/<x>``: only the study calls make and remove these, so no file is written there (it would block a study's folder) and none is deleted.

#### data_rel

```python
data_rel(rel: str | None, *, write: bool, allow_empty: bool = False) -> str
```

A path in a plugin's folder as a plugin or its workspace may name it.

#### class PluginData

One plugin's folder in one project. Created on first write.

- `from_scope(scope: Mapping[str, Any]) -> PluginData`: The calling plugin's folder in the call's project (a service method's scope).
- `from_env(environ: Mapping[str, str] | None = None) -> PluginData`: The plugin's folder in the project a plugin job runs for: the host sets MAGNUSIM_PROJECT_DIR and MAGNUSIM_PLUGIN_KEY for a plugin's jobs.
- `root() -> Path`
- `path(*parts: str) -> Path`: A path inside this plugin's folder (never outside it).
- `read_json(rel: str, default: Any = None) -> Any`
- `write_json(rel: str, doc: Any) -> None`
- `delete(rel: str) -> None`
- `file_path(rel: str, *, write: bool = False) -> Path`: Where ``rel`` is on disk, after the path rules (:func:`data_rel`); for a write also checked where it lands, so it never reaches a study's record, and a file in a study's folder needs that study (:class:`StudyNotFoundError`).
- `file_info(rel: str) -> FileInfo | None`: A file's rel, size, mtime and etag; None when there is no such file.
- `read_bytes(rel: str) -> bytes | None`: A file's bytes; None when there is no such file.
- `open_bytes(rel: str) -> BinaryIO`: A file opened for reading (a large file, read in pieces). Raises FileNotFoundError when there is none.
- `write_bytes(rel: str, data: bytes | bytearray | memoryview) -> FileInfo`: Save a file in one step (a reader never sees half of it); returns its info.
- `atomic_path(rel: str) -> Iterator[Path]`: A temp path next to ``rel`` for code that writes the file itself (a mesher, an exporter). Write it inside the block; when the block ends it replaces ``rel`` in one step. The temp (``.magnusim-<hex>.part`` plus ``rel``'s extension, so a writer that picks its format from the name still does) is removed when the block raises::
- `list_files(prefix: str = "") -> list[FileInfo]`: Every file under ``prefix`` (a folder; "" is the plugin's folder), sorted by rel. Never follows a link or junction, and leaves out the host's temp and staging files. A missing folder lists nothing.
- `usage(limit: int = MAX_ENTRIES) -> tuple[int, int]`: (bytes in files, files and folders) in this plugin's folder, as the host's quota counts them: no link followed, and none of the host's own names (``.magnusim*``). Counting stops a little past ``limit`` entries.
- `check_room(target: Path, size: int, max_total_bytes: int) -> None`: The host's check before a workspace writes ``size`` bytes at ``target`` (``ws.data``): the plugin's ``[files] max_total_mb`` and :data:`MAX_ENTRIES` hold for the whole folder, as for ``ws.files``. Raises ``quota``.
- `delete_file(rel: str, *, recursive: bool = False) -> int`: Delete a file, or a folder and everything in it when ``recursive``. Returns how many files went (0 when there was nothing). A link or junction is removed itself, never what it points to. A study's record and its folder go only through the study calls.
- `studies() -> list[dict[str, Any]]`
- `study(sid: str) -> dict[str, Any]`
- `create_study(kind: str, title: str, *, plugin_name: str = "", plugin_version: str = "0.0.0", schema_version: int = 1) -> dict[str, Any]`
- `update_study(sid: str, patch: dict[str, Any], rev: int | None) -> dict[str, Any]`
- `rename_study(sid: str, title: str, rev: int | None) -> dict[str, Any]`
- `delete_study(sid: str) -> None`

Plugin keys that have a data folder in this project (enabled or not).

## 5. The analysis contract

Contract version 1.4 (`cfddesk.registry.contract`).

The analysis contract (API 1.1): how the core talks to a simulation type.

The core never reaches into an analysis's physics. For every step it calls
one of the functions below, which call the analysis's own hook when it has
one and otherwise fall back to a neutral default:

- :func:`describe_extra`: what the Create modal, the study panel and the run
  panel show about the analysis (family title and tags, algorithm label,
  residual series, x axis, result fields, UI panels).
- :func:`study_defaults` and :func:`sibling`: a new study's settings, and the
  analysis of the same family for the other time dependency.
- :func:`validate_ready`: what still blocks a run, as
  ``[{"message", "fix"}]`` (empty when the run can start).
- :func:`run_defaults`, :func:`run_normalize`, :func:`run_preview`: the run
  settings model (iterations, or simulated time and time step).
- :func:`launch_spec`: which program runs the case, how many frames are
  kept, which processes belong to it and how it is stopped.
- :func:`log_parser_ref`: the module that turns the solver's output into job
  events (the one parser; Node only aggregates events).

Hooks live on :class:`~cfddesk.registry.analysis.AnalysisType` as optional
fields, so a plugin that clones a builtin with ``dataclasses.replace`` keeps
the builtin's behaviour.

### AnalysisType

Registered analysis / physics type (incompressible, CHT, ...).

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `str` |  |  |
| `label` | `str` |  |  |
| `category` | `str` |  |  |
| `time_dependency` | `TimeDependency` |  |  |
| `fields` | `tuple[str, ...]` |  |  |
| `turbulence_models` | `tuple[str, ...]` | `()` | API 1.0, accepted; the core reads only default_turbulence (study seed). |
| `default_turbulence` | `str` | `""` | API 1.0, accepted; the core reads it only to seed a new study's turbulence_model when the analysis's study_defaults leaves it out. |
| `bc_types` | `tuple[str, ...]` | `()` |  |
| `material_models` | `tuple[str, ...]` | `()` |  |
| `solver_backends` | `tuple[str, ...]` | `()` |  |
| `default_solver` | `str` | `""` |  |
| `monitors` | `tuple[str, ...]` | `()` |  |
| `result_fields` | `tuple[ResultField, ...]` | `()` |  |
| `settings_schema` | `tuple[SchemaField, ...]` | `()` |  |
| `numerics_schema` | `tuple[SchemaField, ...]` | `()` |  |
| `control_schema` | `tuple[SchemaField, ...]` | `()` |  |
| `validate` | `Callable[..., list[str]]` | `_no_checks` | API 1.0, accepted; called only through run_analysis_validate (what blocks a run is validate_ready). |
| `region_roles` | `tuple[str, ...]` | `("fluid",)` |  |
| `write_case` | `Callable[[CaseContext], Any] \| None` | `None` |  |
| `parse_log_line` | `Callable[[str], Any] \| None` | `None` | API 1.0, accepted and not read (the solver output parser is log_parser). |
| `requires` | `tuple[Requirement, ...]` | `()` |  |
| `family` | `Any` | `None` | Contract 1.1 (cfddesk.registry.contract). All optional: the core falls back to a neutral default for any hook an analysis leaves out. |
| `algorithm_label` | `str` | `""` |  |
| `residual_keys` | `tuple[str, ...]` | `()` |  |
| `residual_series` | `tuple[dict[str, Any], ...]` | `()` | How the run panel draws them: {key, label, color, fields?, always?, dashed?, max_key?, max_label?, swatch?} per series (contract.residual_series). |
| `x_axis` | `str` | `""` |  |
| `study_defaults` | `Callable[[str], dict[str, Any]] \| None` | `None` |  |
| `validate_ready` | `Callable[[Any], list[Any]] \| None` | `None` |  |
| `run_model` | `Any` | `None` |  |
| `launch` | `Callable[..., Any] \| None` | `None` |  |
| `log_parser` | `Any` | `None` |  |
| `frame_fields` | `tuple[str, ...]` | `()` |  |
| `kinematic_fields` | `tuple[str, ...] \| None` | `None` | Contract 1.4: fields its cases store divided by density (shown times rho). None = not declared (the case's sidecar keeps what write_case put there); () = none. |
| `plan_case` | `Callable[[Any], dict[str, Any]] \| None` | `None` |  |
| `run_monitors` | `Callable[[Any], dict[str, Any]] \| None` | `None` |  |
| `ui` | `dict[str, str]` | `field(default_factory=dict)` |  |
| `monitor_quantities` | `tuple[Any, ...] \| None` | `None` | Contract 1.4: the quantities its run_monitors series carry (MonitorQuantity rows). None = not declared (an analysis with a run_monitors hook gets contract.LEGACY_MONITOR_QUANTITIES); () = none. |

## 6. Hooks

The host fires these (host API 1.4): `case.write`, `case.written`, `solve.parse_line`, `solve.prepare`, `solve.stop`, `ui.tree.transform`.

Reserved (a plugin may listen; they never fire yet): `analysis.validate`, `case.write_field`, `geometry.import`, `geometry.preview`, `mesh.fingerprint`, `mesh.generate`, `mesh.result`, `project.load`, `project.migrate`, `project.save`, `results.filter`, `results.load`.
